title: Typing Performance Hooks
description: Learn how to type useMemo, useCallback, and memo for optimized React components.

data.text: Performance hooks like useMemo and useCallback help avoid unnecessary recalculations. TypeScript ensures the memoized values and callbacks have the correct types.

data.title: Typed useMemo
Typed useCallback

data.text: React.memo wraps a component and prevents re-renders when props haven't changed. With TypeScript, props stay fully typed.

data.title: React.memo
data.content: Memoizing a component with typed props

data.title: Don't Over-Optimize
data.text: useMemo and useCallback add overhead. Profile first, then optimize only when needed. TypeScript helps ensure the optimization is correct.

terms.definition: Memoizes a computed value until dependencies change
Memoizes a function reference until dependencies change
Wraps a component to skip re-renders when props are shallow-equal

items.question: Should I wrap every function in useCallback?
items.answer: No. Only wrap callbacks passed to optimized child components or used as hook dependencies.

items.question: Does useMemo guarantee the same reference?
items.answer: Yes, as long as dependencies don't change. TypeScript ensures the returned type is consistent.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useMemo returns the same type as the computation
Optimize only when profiling shows a benefit
data.takeaway: Typed performance hooks keep optimization safe and maintainable.
